question: A baby born at 36 weeks gestation weighing 1,800 grams is classified as Low Birth Weight (LBW) because birth weight is less than 2,500 grams, regardless of gestational age.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The statement is TRUE. LBW = birth weight <2,500 g, by definition, irrespective of gestational age. This baby is LBW. To determine if the low weight reflects prematurity alone or IUGR/SGA, you plot the weight on a gestational-age-specific growth chart. A 36-week baby weighing 1,800 g may be appropriate for gestational age (AGA preterm) or small for gestational age (SGA), but in either case is LBW by the weight criterion.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! LBW is defined as birth weight <2,500 grams REGARDLESS of gestational age — it is a weight-based definition, not a gestational-age-based one. This baby (36 weeks, 1,800 g) is LBW by weight AND late preterm by gestational age. Sub-classifications: VLBW <1,500 g; ELBW <1,000 g. Determining whether LBW is due to prematurity (AGA for dates) or IUGR (SGA) requires plotting weight on a gestational-age chart.
